Generalized lymphadenopathy is present.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Ch3 style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003EQuestion 4:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/h3\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003EProblem and solution list. Example: problems could be electrolyte imbalance, urosepsis, calculi etc. Solutions would be specific medicines prescribed, dialysis etc. Again.. All cases.. But a lot of them are similar.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003EUROSEPSIS:- is a term used to describe a type of sepsis that is caused by an infection in the urinary tract.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cu\u003ESymptoms of urosepsis include\u003C\/u\u003E:-\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cul style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003Epain near the kidneys, on the lower sides of the back\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003Enausea with or without vomiting\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Eextreme fatigue\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Ereduced urine volume or no urine\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Etrouble breathing or rapid breathing\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Econfusion or brain for\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Eunusual anxiety levels\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Echanges in heart rate, such as palpitations or a rapid heartbeat\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Ehigh fever or low body temperature\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003EA doctor may diagnose urosepsis after confirming that the person has a UTI, which is done through a simple urine sample. If a UTI has been left untreated or the doctor thinks the infection may have spread, they may order immediate blood tests to help diagnose urosepsis.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cu\u003ETreatment\u003C\/u\u003E:-\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003EIf caught early, UTIs are easy to treat with antibiotics. A person with a UTI also needs to drink plenty of fluids to help flush the urinary tract,it may not respond to antibiotics alone.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003ESome people will need surgery to get rid of the source of an untreated infection completely.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003EELECTROLYTE IMBALANCE:-\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; Patients with chronic renal failure, since there is an absence of renal regulatory mechanisms. In renal failure, acute or chronic, one most commonly sees patients who have a tendency to develop hypervolemia, hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, and bicarbonate deficiency (metabolic acidosis). Sodium is generally retained, but may appear normal, or hyponatremic, because of dilution from fluid retention. Following the relief of a urinary tract obstruction, hypovolemia, hyponatremia (true loss of sodium), hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia, and bicarbonate loss are most apt to occur. Electrolyte imbalances after urinary diversion vary depending on the site of urine diversion.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cu\u003ETreatment\u003C\/u\u003E:-\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003EIntravenous fluids, electrolyte replacement.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003EA Minor electrolyte imbalance may be corrected by diet changes. For example; eating a diet rich in potassium if you have low potassium levels, or restricting your water intake if you have a low blood sodium level.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cu\u003EMost commonly cause:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cul style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003Evomiting\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Ediarrhea\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Enot drinking enough fluids\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Enot eating enough\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Eexcessive sweating\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Ecertain medications, such as laxatives and diuretics\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Eeating disorders\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Eliver or kidney problems\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Ecancer treatment\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Econgestive heart failure\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Ch3 style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003EQuestion 5:\u003C\/h3\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis assignemnt has helped me to understand the process of history taking and discussion with the patient.
